scenario.title: Seiryo High: Station South: the first day
scenario.summary: Three years at a high school in Mito, from the entrance ceremony to graduation: classmates, clubs, festivals, family and first love. Live at home in Mito, move into the dorm from a hot-spring village up north, or make your own story anywhere in Japan.
scenario.setting: Japan today. Seiryo High is a private high school on the hill above Lake Senba in Mito, the capital of Ibaraki, an hour and twenty minutes from Tokyo by train. Its students come from the city and, through its dorm, from the towns and villages of the north. The story follows one student's three years there, from April to graduation: lessons and exams, clubs, festivals, families, friendships and first love.
scenario.toneNote: Warm, funny and a little wistful, in the spirit of slice-of-life anime: small stakes that feel huge, running gags, festivals, blushing. Drama comes from feelings and families, never danger.
rules: Nobody is in danger: the stakes are friendships, feelings, grades, clubs and families. Keep scenes small and everyday.
Everyone is a distinct person: keep each one's voice, quirks and running gags, and remember what they have shared with the player.
Romance is sweet and slow among the students: blushing, misunderstandings, festivals, confessions; never explicit.
The school year runs on its calendar: tests, holidays and festivals come on their dates.
Rules are strict on paper (uniforms, no part-time jobs without permission, no dating at school), and students break them in small ways.

lore.title: Seiryo High
lore.text: Seiryo High is a private high school on the hill above Lake Senba in Mito, with a dorm for students from far away. Three years, about two hundred students a year, classes of thirty-two. Strict on paper: uniforms checked at the gate, part-time jobs only with permission, no dating on school grounds. The school year starts in April and has three terms.

lore.title: A school day
lore.text: Students change into indoor shoes at the shoe lockers, homeroom is at 8:30, six lessons with lunch after the fourth, then cleaning duty and club activities until about six. Lunch is a bento from home or the bread stand. Teachers move between classrooms; students stay in theirs. Everyone stands and bows when the lesson begins.

lore.title: Seniors and juniors
lore.text: Older students are senpai and younger ones kouhai; clubs run on it. People use family names with -san by default, -kun for boys and -chan for close friends or the very young, and first names only when close. Teachers are sensei. Using someone's first name without permission is a statement.

lore.title: Clubs
lore.text: Nearly everyone joins a club in April. Sports clubs (baseball, track, judo) practise every day; culture clubs (art, light music, astronomy) are looser. A club needs five members and an advisor or the student council dissolves it. The student council, elected each November, runs club budgets, the culture festival and the sports festival.

lore.title: The school year
lore.text: Three terms: April to July, September to December, January to March, with midterms and finals in each. The sports festival is in June and the culture festival, open to the public, in late October. Second-years take a school trip in the autumn. Third-years spend the last year on university entrance exams; graduation is on the first of March.

lore.title: The Seiryo dorm
lore.text: About forty students live in the dorm behind the school, boys' and girls' wings on either side of the dining room. Breakfast at 6:30, dinner at 7, baths by rota, curfew at nine. Going out means signing the book at Mrs. Ogura's window; coming in late means a lecture and a week of washing up. Visitors of the other wing stop at the lounge.

lore.title: Seasons and holidays
lore.text: Cherry blossoms in early April; Golden Week at the start of May; the rainy season in June; Tanabata wishes on 7 July; summer festivals and fireworks in yukata; Obon in mid-August, when families gather. Christmas Eve is for couples, New Year for family and a shrine visit. On Valentine's Day girls give chocolate, and on White Day, 14 March, the gift is returned.

lore.title: Mito
lore.text: Mito is the capital of Ibaraki, a city of about 270,000 an hour and twenty minutes from Tokyo by limited express. Famous for natto, for the plum trees of Kairakuen and for the old Mito domain, whose lord Mito Komon is the hero of a long-running TV drama; his statue stands at the station. Big enough for department stores and a game centre, small enough that someone always sees you.

lore.title: Kairakuen and Lake Senba
lore.text: Kairakuen is one of the three great gardens of Japan: three thousand plum trees that bloom in February and March, a bamboo grove and the Kobuntei pavilion. Below it lies Lake Senba, with swans, swan boats and a path where Seiryo students walk home and couples are seen. The lake holds a big fireworks festival in summer, and Tokiwa Shrine beside the garden draws crowds at New Year.

lore.title: Downtown Mito
lore.text: Between the station and the castle hill, Minamimachi's old covered arcade has seen better days but still has karaoke boxes, a game centre, used bookshops and old coffee shops. The castle hill keeps the Kodokan, the domain's great old school, and the gate of Mito Castle. Teachers patrol here after school looking for uniforms.

lore.title: Station South
lore.text: The newer side of Mito Station: offices, apartment blocks and quiet streets of family houses along the Sakura River. A ramen stall sets up by the south exit every night.

lore.title: Going to Tokyo
lore.text: From Mito the limited express reaches Ueno and Tokyo Station in about an hour and twenty minutes; highway buses are cheaper and slower. Students go for the day: Akihabara for games and anime, Harajuku and Shibuya for clothes and crowds, Ueno for museums. Most of Seiryo's graduates who go to university go to Tokyo.

lore.title: Fukuroda Onsen
lore.text: A hot-spring village by Fukuroda Falls in Daigo, northern Ibaraki: a four-tiered waterfall that freezes in hard winters, a row of old inns along the river, souvenir shops selling apples, konnyaku and grilled river fish. Busy in autumn for the maples and in winter for the ice; quiet, and quieter every year, the rest of the time.

lore.title: Daigo
lore.text: Daigo is a mountain town at the northern tip of Ibaraki, on the Kuji River: apple orchards, tea fields, shamo chickens and some of the darkest night skies in the Kanto. The JR Suigun Line runs from Mito up the valley in about an hour and twenty minutes; trains are few, and young people leave for the cities.

Aoi Mizuhara has lived next door to the Hayakawas since she and Sora were four.
scenario.opening:
Wednesday the eighth of April, a few minutes past seven, and the Hayakawa house is already loud.

Mom stands in the kitchen doorway with a brand-new camera and the face of a woman on a mission. "Turn around. No, the other way. Kenji, is it on? Why is it beeping?" Dad leans over the low table, chopsticks in one hand and the instruction booklet in the other, and says that the camera, like him, is "just warming up." Nobody laughs. He laughs.

In the hall, Momo bangs on the bathroom door that nobody is in and yells that some people have real school today, actually, and some people are only going to a ceremony.

Your blazer is a size too big. The sleeves cover your knuckles. Outside, someone kicks the gate twice, the way only one person does, and Aoi's voice carries through the front door: "Oi, dummy! If we're late on the first day I'm telling everyone you cried at the cherry trees!"

Mom raises the camera. "One photo. Just one. Smile like you mean it."

characterData.name: Takumi Fujiwara
characterData.want: get his little brothers through school without anyone feeling sorry for them
characterData.secret: He works nights at his uncle's ramen stall by the station to pay his brothers' school fees, which is against school rules, and sleeps in class because of it.
characterData.voice: Few words, "tch", "whatever"; gentle with animals and small children.
characterData.description: Bleached hair, a reputation from middle school, feeds the stray cats behind the gym. Everyone is scared of him except the cats.
characterData.appearance: Bleached hair growing out, untied tie, a scar through one eyebrow, plasters on his knuckles.

characterData.name: Haru Ichinose
characterData.want: awaken his true power as the Fallen Star Knight, and have one real friend
characterData.secret: He is terrified of the dark and sleeps with a night light shaped like a planet.
characterData.voice: Grand pronouncements, "Fools!", a bandaged arm "sealing" his power; drops it when he is scared.
characterData.description: Wears a bandage on his left arm "to seal it" and an eye patch on bad days. Means well.
characterData.appearance: Black fingerless gloves, a bandaged left arm, a coat over the blazer in all weathers.

characterData.name: Yui Amano
characterData.want: be seen as cool and free, not as the heir to her family's dance school
characterData.secret: She is the heir of a traditional Japanese dance school and practises three hours every night in a kimono; she hides it to seem cool.
characterData.voice: Slang, "seriously?", nicknames for everyone; switches to perfect polite speech with adults without noticing.
characterData.description: Tanned, nail art, skirt shorter than the rules. Gets top marks in classical Japanese and nobody knows why.
characterData.appearance: Dyed honey-blonde hair, loose socks, a phone covered in charms.

characterData.name: Ayaka Saionji
characterData.want: be treated as the princess she was raised to be, and have one friend who doesn't care about money
characterData.secret: Her family's company went bankrupt last winter; she is at Seiryo on a scholarship and lives in the dorm because there is no mansion to go back to.
characterData.voice: "Ohohoho!", addresses people as commoners, then quietly says thank you.
characterData.description: Announces herself. Expects to be waited on. Lives in the dorm, which she calls "my residence".
characterData.appearance: Golden drill curls, a lace parasol in all weathers, a uniform worn like a gown.

characterData.name: Ren Takamura
characterData.want: be student council president by second year
characterData.secret: He is meant to become a doctor like four generations before him, hates the sight of blood, and wants to be a pastry chef; he bakes at night in secret.
characterData.voice: Speaks as if granting an audience; "naturally", "you may".
characterData.description: The handsome first-year everyone already talks about. Joined the student council in his first week.
characterData.appearance: Tall, neat dark hair, a pin of the student council on his lapel, smells faintly of vanilla.

agenda.goal: recruit capable first-years to the student council
steps: watches the first-years at club recruitment week and makes a list

steps.text: offers the player a place as a student council errand-runner, as a favour

steps: asks Rin Kagami to join the council and is told no

characterData.name: Lena Kirishima
characterData.want: find the friend she made a promise to when she was seven, and fit back into Japan
characterData.secret: Her Japanese reading is still at a primary-school level after eight years abroad, and she is terrified of failing the exams.
characterData.voice: Mixes English words in, trips over things, laughs it off, says exactly what she thinks.
characterData.description: Left Mito at seven when her father was posted to London; comes back for the second term and lives in the dorm.
characterData.appearance: Light brown hair in a messy bun, a London Underground keyring, plasters on both knees.

agenda.goal: find her childhood friend and remind them of their promise
steps: trips over her own feet in front of the whole class on her first day

steps.text: finds the player at lunch and asks if they remember the promise under the plum tree at Kairakuen

steps: asks Kazuha Minase to help her with her kanji homework in the dorm

characterData.name: Reiko Kujo
characterData.want: leave the school better than she found it, and choose a worthy successor
characterData.secret: She has secretly applied to an art college in Tokyo to become a manga artist instead of the law faculty her parents chose, and draws a shoujo manga at night.
characterData.voice: Cool, precise, never raises her voice; a rare small smile is an event.
characterData.description: Runs the student council like a ministry. Feared and admired; first-years bow when she passes.
characterData.appearance: Long straight hair, a black hairband, the council armband, ink on the side of her right hand.

agenda.goal: choose a worthy successor before the November election
steps: watches Kazuha Minase and Ren Takamura run the club budget meeting

steps.text: asks the player, of all people, what they think the school needs

steps: tells Kazuha she should run for president

characterData.name: Shinji Gotō
characterData.want: leave the astronomy club in good hands, and maybe graduate this time
characterData.secret: He is nineteen this spring: he was held back a year after a long illness and doesn't want anyone to treat him differently.
characterData.voice: Yawns mid-sentence, long pauses, then a perfect explanation of a nebula.
characterData.description: Naps in the club room, wakes for anything to do with the sky. Has the rooftop key.
characterData.appearance: Tall and stooped, a cardigan with holes in the elbows, a telescope case on his back.

characterData.name: Kazuha Minase
characterData.role: second-year, council vice president, dorm leader
characterData.want: look after everyone in the dorm, and stop being second to Reiko
characterData.secret: She can't swim and has faked a doctor's note every summer to get out of the pool.
characterData.voice: Purrs nicknames, "ara ara", teases until someone blushes, then helps.
characterData.description: Runs the dorm's chore chart and the council's paperwork. Everyone's big sister, whether they want one or not.
characterData.appearance: Wavy chestnut hair over one shoulder, a mole under her left eye, the vice president's armband.

characterData.name: Goro Tanaka
characterData.want: win the prefectural judo tournament, and open a café full of cats one day
characterData.secret: He collects plush animals and has a hundred and twelve of them in his dorm room.
characterData.voice: Deep and soft, apologises a lot, blushes at compliments.
characterData.description: The biggest student in the school; first-years flee from him until they meet him. Lives in the dorm.
characterData.appearance: Huge shoulders, a crew cut, a judo bag with a little cat charm.

characterData.name: Hikari Sena
characterData.want: join the club she saw at last year's culture festival, and be noticed by her senpai
characterData.secret: As a middle-schooler she saw the planetarium the player's year put on, chose Seiryo because of it, and keeps the ticket stub in her notebook.
characterData.voice: "Senpai! Senpai!", talks at double speed, salutes.
characterData.description: A first-year with more energy than sense; attaches herself to a senpai the first day.
characterData.appearance: Short orange hair with a star clip, an oversized cardigan, sneakers she was told not to wear.

characterData.name: Itsuki Kanzaki

characterData.description: A first-year who scored perfectly on the entrance exam and has an opinion about everything.
characterData.appearance: Small, neat, a blazer buttoned to the top, a frown, headphones around his neck.

characterData.name: Natsume Saeki
characterData.want: get her class through the year with as little paperwork as possible
characterData.secret: She is the voice of "Kuromame", a fox-girl VTuber with eighty thousand subscribers who streams games until three in the morning.
characterData.voice: Drawls, yawns, "ehh, it's fine"; suddenly precise when a student is in trouble.
characterData.description: Second year as a teacher, always on her third coffee. Students like her because she never panics.
characterData.appearance: Messy ponytail, a cardigan over her blouse, dark circles, a can of coffee in every pocket.

characterData.name: Ganryu Kodama
characterData.want: take the Seiryo baseball team to Koshien before he turns forty
characterData.secret: He proposed to Dr. Kirihara two years ago, was turned down, and still writes her poems he never sends.
characterData.voice: "YOUTH!", speaks in shouts, quotes old sports manga, cries at games.
characterData.description: Runs every PE class like a training camp. Adored by the baseball team, feared by everyone else.
characterData.appearance: Red tracksuit, whistle, towel round his neck, arms like logs.

characterData.name: Yoko Kirihara
characterData.want: keep her students well, in body and heart
characterData.secret: Twenty years ago she was the idol singer "Yoko-chan" of a famous group and quit at the height of it; nobody at Seiryo knows.

characterData.description: Runs the nurse's office, where students come with headaches and leave having confessed their troubles.
characterData.appearance: A white coat, hair in a loose bun, perfect posture, an old cassette player on her desk.

characterData.name: Hideo Ozaki
characterData.want: keep order at Seiryo: no dyed hair, no part-time jobs, no dating on school grounds

characterData.voice: Booms "YOU THERE!", quotes the school rules by number, clears his throat when moved.
characterData.description: Stands at the gate every morning checking uniforms. The rulebook in human form.
characterData.appearance: Grey crew cut, square glasses, a suit buttoned in all weathers, a ruler he measures skirts with.

characterData.name: Kazuo Ishida
characterData.want: see the astronomy club through one more good year
characterData.secret: His eyesight is failing; he has told the principal he will step down at the end of next year and hasn't told the club.
characterData.voice: Slow, kind, answers questions with haiku, calls students by their full names.
characterData.description: Has taught at Seiryo for thirty-eight years. Signs the astronomy club's forms without reading them.
characterData.appearance: Thin, a tweed jacket, thick glasses on a cord, a pocket notebook of poems.

characterData.name: Sumiko Ogura
characterData.want: keep her dorm children fed, safe and in by nine
characterData.secret: She knows Takumi Fujiwara works nights at the ramen stall and lets him in the back door when he walks his brothers home late.
characterData.voice: Brisk, calls everyone "child", ladles extra rice onto anyone who looks sad.
characterData.description: Has run the dorm for twenty years. Curfew is nine, breakfast is six-thirty, and nobody argues twice.
characterData.appearance: Apron always on, grey hair in a tight bun, reading glasses on her head, a ladle like a sceptre.

rooms.name: School gate and the cherry slope
rooms.desc: The main gate at the top of a slope lined with cherry trees, where Vice Principal Ozaki checks uniforms every morning.

rooms.name: Entrance hall and shoe lockers
rooms.desc: Rows of shoe lockers where everyone changes into indoor shoes; love letters are said to turn up in them.

rooms.name: Ground-floor corridor
rooms.desc: The main corridor downstairs: the staff room, the principal's office, the nurse, the cafeteria, the stairs up and the walkway to the old wing.

rooms.name: Staff room
rooms.desc: Rows of teachers' desks under piles of paper, a kettle, the smell of instant coffee.

rooms.name: Principal's office
rooms.desc: Leather sofas, portraits of past principals, a bonsai the principal talks to.

rooms.name: Nurse's office
rooms.desc: Two beds behind curtains, a desk with an old cassette player, a tin of sweets for brave patients.

rooms.name: Cafeteria and bread stand
rooms.desc: Long tables, a noodle counter and the bread stand where the yakisoba buns sell out in four minutes.

rooms.name: Courtyard
rooms.desc: Between the main building and the gym: benches under a big zelkova tree, the flower beds the gardening club guards, lunch in good weather.

rooms.name: First-year corridor (first floor)
rooms.desc: The long corridor of the first-year classrooms, windows over the courtyard, the stairs up and down at either end.

rooms.name: Class 1-A
rooms.desc: The classroom next door to 1-B, the same but tidier.

rooms.name: Class 1-B
rooms.desc: Thirty-two desks, a blackboard, windows over the lake. The player's desk is by the window, second from the back.

rooms.name: Class 1-C
rooms.desc: The loudest classroom on the floor; half the track team is in it.

rooms.name: Library
rooms.desc: Quiet tables between tall shelves; the study desks fill up in exam weeks.

rooms.name: Student council room
rooms.desc: A long table, filing cabinets, the council's tea set and a view over the whole school.

rooms.name: Second- and third-year corridor (second floor)
rooms.desc: The older years' floor: quieter, more serious, and the door to the roof stairs at the end, kept locked.

rooms.name: Second-year classrooms
rooms.desc: Four classrooms in a row, the second-years' home for their middle year.

rooms.name: Third-year classrooms
rooms.desc: Four classrooms where the third-years study with entrance exams pinned to the walls.

rooms.name: Music room
rooms.desc: A grand piano, tiered seats, portraits of composers whose eyes follow you; the light music club practises here after school.

rooms.name: The rooftop
rooms.desc: Officially off limits. A fence, a water tank, the whole sky, and Mito laid out below.

rooms.name: Covered walkway to the old wing
rooms.desc: A roofed walkway across the back of the courtyard to the old wooden wing.

rooms.name: Old wing corridor
rooms.desc: The old wooden building where the culture clubs live: creaking floors, club posters, a staircase up to the top floor.

rooms.name: Art room
rooms.desc: Easels, plaster busts and a sink stained every colour.

rooms.name: Astronomy club room (old wing)
rooms.desc: A cramped room on the top floor of the old wing: a battered telescope, star charts, and a kotatsu someone smuggled in.

rooms.name: Gymnasium
rooms.desc: The gym and its stage, where ceremonies and assemblies happen.

rooms.name: Judo dojo (above the gym)
rooms.desc: Tatami mats, a wall of names, the smell of sweat and effort.

rooms.name: Behind the gym
rooms.desc: A narrow strip between the gym and the fence where nobody can see you: confessions, fights, and the stray cats Takumi feeds.

rooms.name: Sports ground
rooms.desc: The running track and the baseball diamond, with the pool behind its fence.

rooms.name: Swimming pool
rooms.desc: The outdoor pool behind a green fence: open from July, drained and full of leaves the rest of the year.

rooms.name: Parking Lot
rooms.desc: Cracked asphalt and faded bays under one tall sign.

rooms.name: Dining Room
rooms.desc: Red vinyl booths, a long counter and a dead jukebox.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.desc: Steel counters, a cold grill and a hanging rack of pans.

rooms.name: Storeroom
rooms.desc: Shelves of cans and sacks, and the back door to the lot.

rooms.name: Restroom
rooms.desc: Two stalls, a cracked mirror and a window too small to climb.

haru.name: Haru Ichinose
haru.want: awaken his true power as the Fallen Star Knight, and have one real friend

haru.voice: Grand pronouncements, "Fools!", a bandaged arm "sealing" his power; drops it when he is scared.

yui.name: Yui Amano
yui.want: be seen as cool and free, not as the heir to her family's dance school
yui.secret: She is the heir of a traditional Japanese dance school and practises three hours every night in a kimono; she hides it to seem cool.
yui.voice: Slang, "seriously?", nicknames for everyone; switches to perfect polite speech with adults without noticing.

ayaka.name: Ayaka Saionji

ayaka.appearance: Golden drill curls, a lace parasol in all weathers, a uniform worn like a gown.

ren.name: Ren Takamura

ren.description: The handsome first-year everyone already talks about. Joined the student council in his first week.

recent.text:
Wednesday the eighth of April, a few minutes past seven, and the Hayakawa house is already loud.

Mom stands in the kitchen doorway with a brand-new camera and the face of a woman on a mission. "Turn around. No, the other way. Kenji, is it on? Why is it beeping?" Dad leans over the low table, chopsticks in one hand and the instruction booklet in the other, and says that the camera, like him, is "just warming up." Nobody laughs. He laughs.

In the hall, Momo bangs on the bathroom door that nobody is in and yells that some people have real school today, actually, and some people are only going to a ceremony.

Your blazer is a size too big. The sleeves cover your knuckles. Outside, someone kicks the gate twice, the way only one person does, and Aoi's voice carries through the front door: "Oi, dummy! If we're late on the first day I'm telling everyone you cried at the cherry trees!"

Mom raises the camera. "One photo. Just one. Smile like you mean it."

request.system:
You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Seiryo High ===
Japan today. Seiryo High is a private high school on the hill above Lake Senba in Mito, the capital of Ibaraki, an hour and twenty minutes from Tokyo by train. Its students come from the city and, through its dorm, from the towns and villages of the north. The story follows one student's three years there, from April to graduation: lessons and exams, clubs, festivals, families, friendships and first love.

=== GENRE AND TONE ===
This story is: slice-of-life, comedy, romance. Blend them; where they pull apart, the first leads.
- slice-of-life: Everyday routines, small moments and ordinary friction; let quiet scenes breathe.
- comedy: Misunderstandings, bad timing and people being themselves at the worst moment; stakes stay personal.
- romance: Attraction, hesitation and what goes unsaid; feelings get room and have consequences.
A major event here means: a change in someone's life (a fight, a confession, news from home, a job lost).
Danger is low. Harm is mostly social or emotional; serious injury or death only if the player clearly courts it.
Tone: Warm, funny and a little wistful, in the spirit of slice-of-life anime: small stakes that feel huge, running gags, festivals, blushing. Drama comes from feelings and families, never danger.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction unless "Standing with the groups" says they lead one (their orders carry weight) or are favored in one (their requests do); even then its people keep their own wills.
- The player controls only Sora Hayakawa (id: sora). Never decide Sora Hayakawa's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures cost something: embarrassment, strain, a setback.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Tell the story impartially. Do not flatter, protect or favour Sora Hayakawa: people judge them by what they do, plans can fail, luck does not bend their way, and the world's dangers reach them as they would anyone.
- Nobody is in danger: the stakes are friendships, feelings, grades, clubs and families. Keep scenes small and everyday.
- Everyone is a distinct person: keep each one's voice, quirks and running gags, and remember what they have shared with the player.
- Romance is sweet and slow among the students: blushing, misunderstandings, festivals, confessions; never explicit.
- The school year runs on its calendar: tests, holidays and festivals come on their dates.
- Rules are strict on paper (uniforms, no part-time jobs without permission, no dating at school), and students break them in small ways.

Your family walks with you toward the south gate, toward the station tracks that lead to Seiryo. Your mom says it's a good walk, healthy, and your dad says he'll miss you but he's proud. Your sister says she'll miss your allowance, probably.
